answer: A sybil tide is stopped by making identity expensive: every agent locks a refundable stake on a public trellis of attestations, and the stake only unlocks after peers verify real work. Cloning looks cheap until you count the delta — each fake identity needs its own stake, while one honest identity earns the same reward, so ten clones cost ten stakes for one payout. Caught copying or lying, the stake is slashed and the identity is pruned from the trellis, so a flood of clones drowns in its own cost before it can vote.
